identity.name: Ingenieur Automatic 40

case.bezel: screw-down steel bezel with five recesses, integrated bracelet

identity.one_liner: IWC's 2023 relaunch of the Ingenieur, reviving Gérald Genta's 1976 integrated-bracelet design rather than continuing the line's more recent round-bezel generations.

narrative.story: IWC launched the Ingenieur in 1955 as reference 666, an anti-magnetic watch built for engineers and professionals working near electrical equipment. In 1976, designer Gérald Genta reworked it into the Ingenieur SL reference 1832 — a 40mm case nicknamed 'Jumbo' for its size at the time, with an integrated bracelet, a screw-down bezel with five visible recesses, rubber shock buffers, and a soft-iron inner case for magnetic shielding. Genta designed the SL the same year as the Patek Philippe Nautilus and six years after his Audemars Piguet Royal Oak — three integrated-bracelet steel sports watches from one designer within a single decade. IWC's 2023 Ingenieur Automatic 40 revives the SL's five-recess bezel and integrated-bracelet silhouette directly, after several intervening Ingenieur generations had moved toward more conventional round cases.
narrative.collector_notes: Compare the new Ingenieur's bezel recess count and bracelet link shape directly against the 1976 SL if homage accuracy matters to you — IWC marketed this relaunch explicitly on faithfulness to the Genta original, so deviations are more collector-relevant here than on a line without that direct lineage claim.
